claim: Busulfan treatment ablates hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) but leaves compartments of committed lineages intact, including thymic and peripheral T cells.
source: Briefly, we condition young adult CD45.1 hosts with the chemotherapeutic drug busulfan that ablates haematopoetic stem cells (HSC) but leaves compartments of committed lineages intact, including thymic and peripheral T cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the methods description of the busulfan chimera protocol.

claim: By 6 weeks post-BMT, the CD45.1:CD45.2 ratio equilibrates in all thymic compartments.
source: Total numbers of thymocytes remain normal, and by 6 weeks the CD45.1:CD45.2 ratio equilibrates in all thymic compartments (Hogan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by Hogan et al., 2015.

claim: There is no trend in thymic chimerism across treated animals out to a year post-BMT.
source: We see no trend in thymic chimerism across treated animals out to a year post-BMT (Hogan et al., 2015), indicating that chimerism among T cell precursors is stably maintained.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hogan et al., 2015.

claim: Chimeric mice exhibit normal numbers of peripheral CD4 naive and CD4 memory T cells.
source: Chimeric mice also exhibit normal numbers of peripheral CD4 naive and CD4 memory T cells (Figure 1B), and both populations display normal levels of proliferation as assessed by Ki67 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: Both naive and memory CD4 T cell populations in chimeric mice display normal levels of proliferation as assessed by Ki67 expression.
source: Chimeric mice also exhibit normal numbers of peripheral CD4 naive and CD4 memory T cells (Figure 1B), and both populations display normal levels of proliferation as assessed by Ki67 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C comparing chimeras to WT controls.

claim: Busulfan treatment and generation of bone marrow chimerism have no meaningful impact on lymphocyte homeostasis.
source: Together these data indicate that busulfan treatment and the generation of bone marrow chimerism have no meaningful impact on lymphocyte homeostasis, as previously described (Vezys et al., 2006; Hogan et al., 2015).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the data presented and supported by citations to Vezys et al., 2006 and Hogan et al., 2015.

claim: By 8 weeks post-BMT, donor-derived cells are readily detectable in both the naive and CD44hi memory compartments.
source: By 8 weeks post-BMT, donor-derived cells are readily detectable not only in the naive but also to a striking extent in the CD44hi memory compartment (Figure 1D), revealing that well into adulthood newly generated naive T cells continue to differentiate into memory in clean healthy mice.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Well into adulthood, newly generated naive T cells continue to differentiate into memory in clean healthy mice.
source: By 8 weeks post-BMT, donor-derived cells are readily detectable not only in the naive but also to a striking extent in the CD44hi memory compartment (Figure 1D), revealing that well into adulthood newly generated naive T cells continue to differentiate into memory in clean healthy mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of donor-derived cells in memory compartments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: There is steady but ultimately incomplete replacement of host-derived CD4 memory cells with donor cells over the course of a year.
source: We observe a steady but ultimately incomplete replacement of the host-derived CD4 memory cells with donor cells over the course of a year (Figure 1E), while the total CD4 memory compartment remains relatively stable in size (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The total CD4 memory compartment remains relatively stable in size over the course of a year in busulfan chimeras.
source: We observe a steady but ultimately incomplete replacement of the host-derived CD4 memory cells with donor cells over the course of a year (Figure 1E), while the total CD4 memory compartment remains relatively stable in size (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The appearance of donor CD4 TEM cells lagged that of both naive and TCM cells.
source: First, the appearance of donor CD4 TEM cells lagged that of both naive and TCM cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that CD4 TCM are sourced predominantly from naive precursors while CD4 TEM may be sourced either directly from the naive compartment and/or via CD4 TCM.
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD4 TCM are sourced predominantly from naive precursors.
source: First, the appearance of donor CD4 TEM cells lagged that of both naive and TCM cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that CD4 TCM are sourced predominantly from naive precursors while CD4 TEM may be sourced either directly from the naive compartment and/or via CD4 TCM.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetics of donor cell appearance shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD4 TEM may be sourced either directly from the naive compartment and/or via CD4 TCM.
source: First, the appearance of donor CD4 TEM cells lagged that of both naive and TCM cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that CD4 TCM are sourced predominantly from naive precursors while CD4 TEM may be sourced either directly from the naive compartment and/or via CD4 TCM.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetics of donor cell appearance shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Donor cells displayed a more restricted capacity for populating memory relative to the naive pool.
source: Second, donor cells displayed a more restricted capacity for populating memory relative to the naive pool (Figure 1E).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Naive T cell numbers, and not CD4 TCM numbers, provide the strongest predictor of CD4 TEM accumulation over long timescales.
source: Thus, naive T cell numbers, and not CD4 TCM numbers, provide the strongest predictor of CD4 TEM accumulation over long timescales.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the statistical comparison of models.

claim: For CD4 TEM, comparable statistical support was found for the resistant memory and declining recruitment models (ΔAIC = 0.16).
source: For CD4 TEM we found comparable statistical support for the resistant memory and declining recruitment models (ΔAIC = 0.16).
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of model fits.

claim: For CD4 TCM, stronger support was found for the resistant memory model (ΔAIC = 8.3).
source: For CD4 TCM we found stronger support for the resistant memory model (ΔAIC = 8.3).
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of model fits.

claim: In 14 week-old mice, 6.3% of CD4 TEM (95% confidence interval 4.4–8.6) are displaced per week by new memory cells from the source.
source: We estimate that in 14 week-old mice, 6.3% of CD4 TEM (95% confidence interval 4.4–8.6) and 9.8% (6.5–16.9) of CD4 TCM are displaced per week by new memory cells from the source.
evidence: This is an estimate derived from fitting the resistant memory model to the data.

claim: In 14 week-old mice, 9.8% (95% confidence interval 6.5–16.9) of CD4 TCM are displaced per week by new memory cells from the source.
source: We estimate that in 14 week-old mice, 6.3% of CD4 TEM (95% confidence interval 4.4–8.6) and 9.8% (6.5–16.9) of CD4 TCM are displaced per week by new memory cells from the source.
evidence: This is an estimate derived from fitting the resistant memory model to the data.

claim: Between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the proportion of CD4 TEM cells replaced each week by new memory falls from 6.3% to 1%.
source: We predict that between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the proportion of cells replaced each week by new memory falls from 6.3% to 1% for CD4 TEM and 9.8% to 6% for CD4 TCM.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model based on the data.

claim: Between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the proportion of CD4 TCM cells replaced each week by new memory falls from 9.8% to 6%.
source: We predict that between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the proportion of cells replaced each week by new memory falls from 6.3% to 1% for CD4 TEM and 9.8% to 6% for CD4 TCM.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model based on the data.

claim: Between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the resistant, numerically stable memory populations make up 16% to 40% of CD4 TCM.
source: Finally, we estimate that between 14 weeks and 1 year of age the resistant, numerically stable memory populations make up 16% to 40% of CD4 TCM and 96% to 46% of CD4 TEM, though with some uncertainty (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an estimate from the model shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Between 14 weeks and 1 year of age, the resistant, numerically stable memory populations make up 96% to 46% of CD4 TEM.
source: Finally, we estimate that between 14 weeks and 1 year of age the resistant, numerically stable memory populations make up 16% to 40% of CD4 TCM and 96% to 46% of CD4 TEM, though with some uncertainty (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an estimate from the model shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Throughout the period from 14 weeks to 1 year of age, approximately 10% of the displaceable CD4 TCM subpopulation is replaced each week.
source: Throughout this period approximately 10% of the remaining displaceable CD4 TCM subpopulation is replaced each week.
evidence: This is an estimate from the model.

claim: At 14 weeks of age, as much as 65% of displaceable CD4 TEM are replaced per week.
source: For CD4 TEM, because the resistant population at 14 weeks of age is estimated to be a large proportion of the pool and the source is substantial, we predict that as much 65% of displaceable CD4 TEM are replaced per week.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model.

claim: The rate of displaceable CD4 TEM replacement falls to 1.5%/week in year-old mice.
source: This rate falls to 1.5 %/week in year-old mice as the displaceable population grows and the rate of immigration falls in tandem with naive T cell numbers (Figure 2D, right-hand panels).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Ki67 is a nuclear protein that is expressed during cell division but subsequently lost by non-dividing cells on a timescale of a few days.
source: Ki67 is a nuclear protein that is expressed during cell division but subsequently lost by non-dividing cells on a timescale of a few days (Pitcher et al., 2002; Younes et al., 2011; De Boer and Perelson, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pitcher et al., 2002; Younes et al., 2011; De Boer and Perelson, 2013.

claim: Over the relatively short time courses of the BrdU experiments, there were no substantial changes in either the absolute sizes of memory T cell subsets or in the fraction of cells expressing Ki67.
source: Over the relatively short time courses of the experiments we saw no substantial changes in either the absolute sizes of memory T cell subsets or in the fraction of cells expressing Ki67 (Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1.

claim: The data showed unequivocal support for kinetic over pure temporal heterogeneity within the CD4 effector and central memory pools (ΔAIC = 110 for CD4 TEM, 251 for CD4 TCM).
source: Strikingly, despite this freedom in parameterisation, the data were sufficiently rich to discriminate between the models and showed unequivocal support for kinetic over pure temporal heterogeneity within the CD4 effector and central memory pools (Figure 4, ΔAIC = 110 (CD4 TEM), 251 (CD4 TCM)).
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of model fits shown in Figure 4.

claim: For both memory subsets, the BrdU/Ki67 timecourses were consistent with the existence of two subpopulations roughly equal in size but with highly distinct kinetics.
source: For both memory subsets the BrdU/Ki67 timecourses were consistent with the existence of two subpopulations roughly equal in size but with highly distinct kinetics (Table 2 and Figure 5A, at dashed vertical lines).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the model fits to the data shown in Table 2 and Figure 5A.

claim: CD4 TCM comprise a population dividing and dying roughly every 3 days, and a slower population with mean lifetime of 38 days, dividing every 170 days.
source: CD4 TCM appear to comprise a population dividing and dying roughly every 3 days, and a slower population with mean lifetime of 38 days, dividing every 170 days, with the source feeding the slow and fast populations in roughly a 2:1 ratio.
evidence: These are parameter estimates from the kinetic heterogeneity model fit to the data.

claim: For CD4 TCM, the source feeds the slow and fast populations in roughly a 2:1 ratio.
source: CD4 TCM appear to comprise a population dividing and dying roughly every 3 days, and a slower population with mean lifetime of 38 days, dividing every 170 days, with the source feeding the slow and fast populations in roughly a 2:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a parameter estimate from the kinetic heterogeneity model fit to the data.

claim: For CD4 TEM, the fast population is essentially self-renewing, dividing and dying every 6 days.
source: For CD4 TEM the fast population appears to be essentially self-renewing, dividing and dying every 6 days, with the slower population fed by the source (mean lifetime 43 days, interdivision time 140 days).
evidence: These are parameter estimates from the kinetic heterogeneity model fit to the data.

claim: For CD4 TEM, the slower population is fed by the source and has a mean lifetime of 43 days and interdivision time of 140 days.
source: For CD4 TEM the fast population appears to be essentially self-renewing, dividing and dying every 6 days, with the slower population fed by the source (mean lifetime 43 days, interdivision time 140 days).
evidence: These are parameter estimates from the kinetic heterogeneity model fit to the data.

claim: If the contribution of the source is neglected, pool-averaged cell lifetimes may be overestimated by 25–50%.
source: The flows into memory impact measures of homeostatic dynamics significantly; if the contribution of the source is neglected, pool-averaged cell lifetimes may be overestimated by 25–50% and, more strikingly, interdivision times underestimated by a factor of 2–3 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by comparing parameter estimates with and without a source term in Figure 5A.

claim: If the contribution of the source is neglected, interdivision times may be underestimated by a factor of 2–3.
source: The flows into memory impact measures of homeostatic dynamics significantly; if the contribution of the source is neglected, pool-averaged cell lifetimes may be overestimated by 25–50% and, more strikingly, interdivision times underestimated by a factor of 2–3 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by comparing parameter estimates with and without a source term in Figure 5A.

claim: At the best estimates of the influx into CD4 TEM and TCM from the naive pool, the influx predominantly feeds the slower subpopulations within each.
source: At our best estimates of the influx into CD4 TEM and TCM from the naive pool, we infer that it predominantly feeds the slower subpopulations within each.
evidence: This is inferred from the model fits to the data.

claim: For CD4 TCM, almost equal support was found for a model in which Ki67high cells died 10 times faster than Ki67low cells and for the basic KH model in which death rates are independent of Ki67 expression level.
source: For CD4 TCM we found almost equal support for a model in which Ki67high cells died 10 times faster than Ki67low cells and for the basic KH model in which death rates are independent of the level of Ki67 expression.
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of model fits.

claim: The data do not provide evidence for substantial differences in the susceptibility to death of recently-divided and quiescent memory CD4 T cells.
source: We conclude that our data do not provide evidence for substantial differences in the susceptibility to death of recently-divided and quiescent memory CD4 T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the model comparison results.

claim: The mean post-mitotic duration of Ki67 expression was estimated to be between 3.1 and 3.7 days.
source: We estimated the mean post-mitotic duration of Ki67 expression to be between 3.1 and 3.7 days, consistent with estimates elsewhere (Pitcher et al., 2002; Younes et al., 2011; De Boer and Perelson, 2013).
evidence: This is an estimate from the model fits, consistent with cited literature.

claim: The estimate of Ki67 expression duration was model-independent, insensitive to the magnitude of the influx into memory, and closely comparable for CD4 TEM and TCM.
source: This estimate was model-independent, insensitive to the magnitude of the influx into memory, and closely comparable for CD4 TEM and TCM (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The KH model predicted that the fast subpopulations express Ki67 at levels of approximately 65% (CD4 TEM) and 85% (TCM).
source: The KH model predicted that the fast subpopulations express Ki67 at levels of approximately 65% (CD4 TEM) and 85% (TCM), while the slow populations in both are less than 10% Ki67high (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a prediction from the kinetic heterogeneity model shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The slow populations in both CD4 TEM and TCM are less than 10% Ki67high.
source: The KH model predicted that the fast subpopulations express Ki67 at levels of approximately 65% (CD4 TEM) and 85% (TCM), while the slow populations in both are less than 10% Ki67high (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a prediction from the kinetic heterogeneity model shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ki67high CD4 memory cells are highly enriched for the fast dividing subset.
source: Ki67high CD4 memory cells are therefore predicted to be highly enriched for the fast dividing subset.
evidence: This is inferred from the model predictions of Ki67 expression levels in fast and slow subpopulations.

claim: The relative sizes of the fast and slow subsets were similar to the split of donor/host cells observed in memory in the busulfan chimeras.
source: Notably, the relative sizes of the fast and slow subsets were similar to the split of donor/host cells observed in memory in the busulfan chimeras (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation comparing model predictions to data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Donor cells were slightly enriched for Ki67high cells relative to host cells in busulfan chimeras 8 weeks after BMT.
source: Although donor cells were indeed slightly enriched for Ki67high cells relative to host cells, both subpopulations exhibited substantial levels of Ki67 expression (Figure 5D) and did not map to the fast/slow populations inferred from the BrdU labelling analysis.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Both newly-recruited donor and more established host memory CD4 T cells are kinetically heterogeneous.
source: These data therefore strongly suggest that both newly-recruited donor and more established host memory CD4 T cells are kinetically heterogeneous.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Ki67 expression data in donor and host cells shown in Figure 5D.

claim: There is strong evidence for rapidly- and slowly-dividing populations within both effector and central CD4 memory T cells in uninfected adult mice.
source: In summary, we find strong evidence for rapidly- and slowly-dividing populations within both effector and central CD4 memory T cells in uninfected adult mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the BrdU/Ki67 labelling data and model fits.

claim: There is no strong evidence for recent division impacting susceptibility to cell death in memory CD4 T cells.
source: We find no strong evidence for recent division impacting susceptibility to cell death.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the model comparison results.

claim: Accounting for the constitutive flows of cells into both memory subsets significantly improves the description of BrdU labelling kinetics.
source: Accounting for the constitutive flows of cells into both memory subsets significantly improves the description of BrdU labelling kinetics, and strongly impacts estimates of rates of memory T cell division and turnover.
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of models with and without a source term.

claim: Accounting for the constitutive flows of cells into memory subsets strongly impacts estimates of rates of memory T cell division and turnover.
source: Accounting for the constitutive flows of cells into both memory subsets significantly improves the description of BrdU labelling kinetics, and strongly impacts estimates of rates of memory T cell division and turnover.
evidence: This is shown by comparing parameter estimates with and without a source term (Figure 5A).

claim: The estimated average lifetimes of lymph-node-derived memory CD4 T cells are 21 days for TCM and 29 days for TEM.
source: Our estimated average lifetimes of lymph-node-derived memory CD4 T cells (21d for TCM and 29d for TEM) are slightly higher than those made previously.
evidence: These are parameter estimates from the kinetic heterogeneity model with source.

claim: Other studies of total CD44hi CD4 T cells using BrdU or deuterated water labelling found kinetics consistent with mean lifetimes of 14-22 days.
source: Other studies of total CD44hi CD4 T cells using BrdU or deuterated water labelling found kinetics consistent with mean lifetimes of 14-22d (De Boer and Perelson, 2013; Westera et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to De Boer and Perelson, 2013 and Westera et al., 2013.

claim: A previous study found that a simple model of two self-renewing, stable populations described CD4 memory labelling kinetics better than the simplest single-compartment model with no temporal heterogeneity.
source: One of these studies found that a simple model of two self-renewing, stable populations described the labelling kinetics better than the simplest single-compartment model with no temporal heterogeneity, and that the fast and slow CD4 memory populations were comparable in size (Westera et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Westera et al., 2013.

claim: Studies assuming memory is a self-renewing compartment will tend to overestimate lifetimes and underestimate interdivision times.
source: Thus, studies assuming memory is a self-renewing compartment will tend to overestimate lifetimes and underestimate interdivision times.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparing parameter estimates with and without a source term.

claim: Heterogeneity within the CD4 memory compartment as a whole has been recognised for some time, with a distinction drawn between slow-dividing cells driven by cytokines and fast-dividing cells.
source: Heterogeneity within the CD4 memory compartment as a whole has been recognised for some time, with a distinction drawn between slow-dividing cells driven by cytokines (Seddon et al., 2003; Purton et al., 2007) and in which memory to defined antigens is thought to reside, and fast-dividing cells (Tough and Sprent, 1994; Robertson et al., 2006; Purton et al., 2007; Surh and Sprent, 2008; Younes et al., 2011) whose proliferation is dependent on TCR signalling (Min et al., 2003; Seddon et al., 2003; Leignadier et al., 2008; Younes et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Ki67 expression levels in the slower-dividing populations are approximately 9–11%.
source: We infer that Ki67 expression levels in the slower-dividing populations are approximately 9–11% (Figure 5C), consistent with direct observations of antigen-specific CD4 memory (Lenz et al., 2004; Purton et al., 2007; Pepper et al., 2010; Younes et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred from the model shown in Figure 5C and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: CD4 TEM and TCM subsets comprise both fast and slow subpopulations.
source: Here, we find evidence that CD4 TEM and TCM subsets comprise both fast and slow subpopulations, suggesting that they are indeed similar in their homeostatic dynamics and structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic heterogeneity model fits to the data.

claim: CD4 TEM and TCM are similar in their homeostatic dynamics and structure.
source: Here, we find evidence that CD4 TEM and TCM subsets comprise both fast and slow subpopulations, suggesting that they are indeed similar in their homeostatic dynamics and structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that both subsets comprise fast and slow subpopulations.

claim: The fast CD4 TCM subpopulation divides approximately every 3 days.
source: The fast CD4 TCM and TEM subpopulations divide approximately every 3 and 6 days respectively, while their slower counterparts divide only every 140 days or more.
evidence: This is a parameter estimate from the kinetic heterogeneity model.

claim: The fast CD4 TEM subpopulation divides approximately every 6 days.
source: The fast CD4 TCM and TEM subpopulations divide approximately every 3 and 6 days respectively, while their slower counterparts divide only every 140 days or more.
evidence: This is a parameter estimate from the kinetic heterogeneity model.

claim: The slower counterparts of CD4 TCM and TEM divide only every 140 days or more.
source: The fast CD4 TCM and TEM subpopulations divide approximately every 3 and 6 days respectively, while their slower counterparts divide only every 140 days or more.
evidence: This is a parameter estimate from the kinetic heterogeneity model.

claim: A substantial fraction of the fast subsets (greater than half for CD4 TCM) will begin to divide again before losing Ki67 expression.
source: Therefore a substantial fraction of the fast subsets (greater than half for CD4 TCM) will begin to divide again before losing Ki67 expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the interdivision times and Ki67 expression duration estimates.

claim: The substantial and tonic de novo generation of memory cells braids into highly dynamic and heterogeneous subpopulations which exhibit an unexpectedly diverse age structure.
source: Taken together, our data reveal complexity in the regulation of memory compartments, in which the substantial and tonic de novo generation of memory cells braids into highly dynamic and heterogeneous subpopulations which themselves exhibit an unexpectedly diverse age structure.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all the data presented.

claim: Despite complexity in cell dynamics, memory compartment sizes are remarkably stable throughout life, indicating tight homeostatic control.
source: Despite this complexity in cell dynamics, the compartment sizes are remarkably stable throughout life, indicating tight homeostatic control.
evidence: This is observed in the data showing stable memory compartment sizes (Figure 1B, Figure 2C).

claim: Both effector and central memory CD4 T cells comprise subpopulations with highly divergent rates of turnover.
source: We find that both effector and central memory CD4 T cells comprise subpopulations with highly divergent rates of turnover, and show that inflows of new cells sourced from the naive pool strongly impact estimates of memory cell lifetimes and division rates.
evidence: This is a main finding from the kinetic heterogeneity model fits to the BrdU/Ki67 data.

claim: Inflows of new cells sourced from the naive pool strongly impact estimates of memory cell lifetimes and division rates.
source: We find that both effector and central memory CD4 T cells comprise subpopulations with highly divergent rates of turnover, and show that inflows of new cells sourced from the naive pool strongly impact estimates of memory cell lifetimes and division rates.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing parameter estimates with and without a source term (Figure 5A).

claim: The maintenance of CD4 T cell memory subsets in healthy mice is unexpectedly and strikingly reliant on replenishment from the naive pool.
source: We also demonstrate that the maintenance of CD4 T cell memory subsets in healthy mice is unexpectedly and strikingly reliant on this replenishment.
evidence: This is a main conclusion from the busulfan chimera experiments showing substantial replacement of memory cells by donor-derived cells (Figure 1, Figure 2).
